# CTPA-Dose-Response

Repository: https://github.com/reblocke/CTPA-Dose-Response
Maintainer: Brian W. Locke, ORCID 0000-0002-3588-5238
License: MIT for repository code and original documentation.

## Purpose

This repository contains legacy analysis code, exploratory notebooks, data documentation, and an unpublished author manuscript draft for a CTPA dose-response analysis of pulmonary artery size and mortality risk.

The project asks whether pulmonary artery diameter (PAd) and pulmonary artery to ascending aorta ratio (PA:AA) have dose-response associations with mortality after emergency-department computed tomography pulmonary angiography, and whether age/sex normalization changes prognostic interpretation.

## Scholarly Status

Primary citable scholarly record:

- Locke BW, Scarpato B, Bledsoe J, Knox D, Conner K, Stoddard GJ, Cirulis MM, Elliott CG, Dodson MW. Pulmonary Artery Size on CT and Mortality Risk: A Dose-Response Analysis. CHEST. 2023;164(4 Suppl):A6004-A6005. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.chest.2023.07.3871
- Public abstract listing: https://reblocke.github.io/talks/

This repository is not tied to a final full journal article. The Markdown manuscript is an unpublished author draft for indexing and review:

- `manuscript/ctpa-dose-response-unpublished-author-draft.md`
- source DOCX: `manuscript/source/2023-10-10-dose-response-letter.docx`

Related background paper, not the primary citation target:

- Scarpato BM, Locke BW, Bledsoe J, et al. The association between pulmonary artery enlargement and mortality in an Emergency Department population undergoing computed tomography pulmonary angiography. Pulmonary Circulation. 2023;13(2):e12225. DOI: https://doi.org/10.1002/pul2.12225

## Data Restrictions

Restricted patient-level clinical imaging/EHR-derived inputs are not public and must not be committed.

Expected local-only inputs:

- `data/private/final_noempi.dta`
- `data/private/cleaned_noempi.dta`
- `data/private/ACCT EMPI BMI Weight Height.csv`

The `noempi` files may be stripped of direct EMPI identifiers but remain patient-level restricted data. Do not add row-level datasets, registry files, PHI, credentials, or collaborator-only materials.

## Workflow

Run from repository root:

```bash
stata-mp -b do "Data_preprocess.do" "data/private" "outputs/stata"
stata-mp -b do "Age-Metric Analysis.do" "data/private" "outputs/stata"
stata-mp -b do "PA Body-size Analysis.do" "data/private" "outputs/stata"
```

Optional legacy combined script:

```bash
stata-mp -b do "BL CombofilewithoutEMPI.do" "data/private" "outputs/stata"
```

Default input root is `data/private`. Default output root is `outputs/stata`. Generated logs, tables, graphs, copied do-files, and derived `.dta` files are written under `outputs/stata/<date>/`.

## Important Files

- `README.md`: human-facing project overview, citation, workflow, data restrictions, and license boundaries.
- `CITATION.cff`: machine-readable repository and CHEST abstract citation metadata.
- `AGENTS.md`: instructions for future coding agents.
- `data_dictionary.md` and `data_dictionary.csv`: expected inputs, derived variables, outcomes, and generated artifacts.
- `Data_preprocess.do`: restricted-data preprocessing and merge workflow.
- `Age-Metric Analysis.do`: main age/sex normalization and dose-response survival workflow.
- `PA Body-size Analysis.do`: body-size and ratio exploratory workflow.
- `age-sex-norm-letter.ipynb` and `ratio_val_analysis.ipynb`: historical exploratory notebooks with cleared outputs.

## Artifact Policy

Third-party reference PDFs and publisher PDFs are not tracked on the branch tip; use DOI links instead. Historical rendered notebook HTML/PDF exports were archived in GitHub release `legacy-rendered-artifacts-2026-06-04`.

Do not treat release artifacts as canonical reproducible outputs. Reruns require restricted local clinical data.

## Agent Cautions

- Do not rewrite scientific analysis logic unless explicitly requested.
- Do not describe the manuscript draft as peer reviewed, accepted, or journal-published.
- Keep the CHEST abstract DOI `10.1016/j.chest.2023.07.3871` as the primary scholarly citation.
- Keep the Pulmonary Circulation DOI `10.1002/pul2.12225` as related background only.
- Preserve no-history-rewrite hygiene: remove unsuitable files from branch tips, but do not rewrite git history unless explicitly instructed.
